answer.rationale: Rollback is unavailable because the in-flight security patch must stay. Circuit breaking would fail settlement writes, which violates the no-lost-writes objective. The symptom is write-path saturation at daily settlement peak, so the closest prior lesson is pre-peak headroom (b3), not a proven regional fault (b2) or dashboard-read offload (b5). Adding capacity is the intervention most likely to keep accepting writes while latency is investigated; b3 and b5 should be source-checked because b3 was timed before a peak (we are already in one) and b5 may not transfer from report reads to settlement writes. Uncertainty remains that this is a release-induced efficiency regression rather than a raw capacity shortfall.
